To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the amount of efforts expended to achieve task completion depends on the language of the task context; (b) the amount of effort expended to achieve task success depends on the language in which the task is presented.
• The choice of language has a significant effect on the amount of user efforts needed to achieve task completion in cross-language retrieval.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How does the user experience of a cross-language information retrieval system vary depending on the task context, language, and user group?
the effects of task context and language on user performance in information retrieval, and the design of user interfaces to support crosslanguage retrieval.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
users need to spend less time to complete a document assessment task if the task is in a language that they are more proficient at.
the amount of effort required to achieve task completion is affected by the choice of language and by the choice of task.

the results of the experiments are inconclusive, which is a good result in itself: we have not been able to prove that cross-language information retrieval is more difficult than monolingual information retrieval.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the choice of language and the task context have effects on the effort users need to expend.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of interactive cross-language retrieval in a simulated task setting and that we have identified a few factors that may influence user performance.
the effects of language and context are more complex than we initially thought, and that there are no simple solutions for the design of interactive cross-language systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the user interface should be adapted to task context.
interactive cross-language retrieval can be made efficient by exploiting the user’s language skills.
the amount of user effort needed to achieve task completion is not only determined by the user’s proficiency in a language, but also depends on the context in which the user is working.
